title: Yet they deny God is the author of sin: he effects only what is positive; the depravity is a privation
source_text: XIX. Inde tamen sequi negant Deum esse peccati authorem: quoniam Deus in actu peccati non aliud efficit quam id quod in eo est positivum, adeoque bonum; ac proinde non ad aliud movet & determinat: pravitas vero & vitiositas quae tali actui adhaeret, non est aliquid positivum, quod opus habeat causa proprie efficiente, sed solum rectitudinis debitae privatio, quae ex defectu creatae Voluntatis oritur.
pass_a_gloss: Yet they deny that it follows thence that God is the author of sin: because God in the act of sin effects nothing else than that which is positive in it, and so good; and accordingly moves and determines to nothing else: but the depravity and viciousness which adheres to such an act, is not something positive, which needs a cause properly efficient, but only the privation of due rectitude, which arises from the defect of the created Will.
pass_b_english: They deny, however, that it follows that God is the author of sin. In an act of sin God brings about only what is positive in it, and therefore good, and moves and determines the will to nothing beyond that.

The depravity and corruption attached to such an act is nothing positive requiring a cause that properly produces it. It is only the absence of the rightness the act ought to have, and it arises from the failure of the created will.

choices.why: Kept as the Thomist technical term; Le Blanc explains 'physical' as opposed to 'moral', not to 'supernatural'.
